messages:
isabel: Heads-up: onboarding hit because our CLI `rw login --project` flow writes REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY into env file and that ended up overriding developers' personal REDWOOD_API_KEY in the sampleapp container. Result: requests suddenly fail with 403 after rotation because project-scoped key lacks necessary org scope.

 tom: Wait, CLI writes env files? Which file and flow? That sounds dangerous.

 isabel: It appends to `/etc/profile.d/redwood.sh` in the container we use for CI, so next shells pick it up. Repro steps in ticket. Logs show permission error when calling embeddings endpoint: 
```
2026-03-10T12:03:21Z error: 403 Forbidden - token missing scope: embeddings.create
client: org=acme-corp project=demo
```

 rachel: Oof. So precedence problem + scope mismatch. SDKs should clearly separate "project-scoped" tokens (for project routing) vs "user-scoped" tokens (org-level). Right now we treat them identically.

 vlad: Agree. Parity concern too: py/go treat REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY as additive metadata but JS currently ignores it and only reads REDWOOD_API_KEY. This mismatch explains why some sampleapps behaved differently across languages.

 isabel: Customer hit was node sampleapp -> 403. Local dev (python sampleapp) worked because py merged project token into headers differently.

 tom: Short-term mitigation: CLI should stop writing env files and instead print export lines and warn. Add `--apply` flag opt-in. Also add `rw login` to write to `~/.redwood/credentials` with explicit keys named `default` and `project:<id>`. That keeps precedence explicit.

 rachel: For SDKs: define clear precedence doc: explicit client config > environment (REDWOOD_API_KEY) > project env (REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY) only used for routing but not to replace main auth > token file > home creds. And, importantly, project key must never downgrade scopes. If project key lacks required scope, SDK should prefer higher-scope key.

 vlad: We also need a consistent header mapping across SDKs: `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and optional `x-redwood-project: <project_id>` when using project-scoped key for routing. That way we don't conflate auth and routing. Update SDKs to emit that header when `REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY` present.

 cli-bot: cli: created issue RW-5123 to stop env file writes and add `--apply` safeguard.

 isabel: Also found a related bug: SDK retry logic for 5xx vs 401 is inconsistent. In JS we retry idempotent requests on 5xx but not embeddings requests (which are non-idempotent) even though we can safely retry with resume token on server side. Need to formalize retry policy per endpoint.

 tom: Good point. Suggestion: server emits `x-retry-safe: true` for endpoints safe to retry and `x-resume-token` when a request can be resumed. SDKs then follow server guidance. For streams, on 401 try a credential reload flow: attempt refresh from sources (env, file, config) up to 3 times with backoff, then reconnect with resume token if provided. Gate behind feature flags `REDWOOD_ENABLE_STREAM_REFRESH` and `REDWOOD_ENABLE_SERVER_RETRY_HEADER`.

 rachel: Action items: vlad -> SDK header parity across languages + PR to add `x-redwood-project` header; tom -> CLI change to avoid env file writes and add `--apply`; isabel -> add repro + customer impact note and request fast rollback plan; infra -> server team to consider `x-retry-safe` and `x-resume-token` headers. We'll mark as P0 DX for affected customer and P1 for general SDK parity. :raised_hands:
